Visual Analytics

Visual analytics combines graphical views with operations that change how data is summarized, organized, selected, and inspected.

Operation Main function Example
Drill Down Change the level of detail Clarity → individual diamond
Sort / Group Reorder or combine categories Rank average prices; combine VS1 and VS2
Set / Filter Define membership or restrict data Color selected IDs; show one rater
Trend / Reference Line Fit a relationship or add a benchmark Price–weight fit; average price
Parameter / Action Use an adjustable value or a selection Change a threshold by typing or clicking
Tooltip / Data Guide Inspect supporting details Read a record; inspect an explanation

Dimensions / Measures — Field Roles

Dimensions partition records into categories: CLARITY, RATER, or individual IDNO values.

Measures provide values to aggregate within those groups: AVG(PRICE), SUM(PRICE).

Data type describes the stored values: number, text, date, and so on.

RoleDisplay choice
DimensionDiscrete; numeric/date dimensions may also be continuous
MeasureContinuous or discrete

A numeric identifier is not an amount to sum. Blue/green is not the Dimension/Measure distinction.

Tableau Help4 / 33
Visual Analytics in TableauIA342 · Week 9

Aggregation and Level of Detail

Columns: AVG(WEIGHT). Rows: AVG(PRICE).

  1. No dimension: one average pair.
  2. RATER / CLARITY on Detail: one pair per category.
  3. IDNO on Detail: one pair per record.

Changing AVG → SUM changes the computation, not the grouping. At one row per ID, both return the same value.

The HTML control replaces the Detail field. In Tableau, remove the old dimension before adding the next.

Some record-level marks overlap.

Discrete / Continuous — Numeric ID

Discrete: separate values with individual headers. Continuous: values located along an axis.
IDNO is a dimension in both views; AVG(PRICE) is the measure. Bar and Line are separate Marks choices.

Drill Down — Date Hierarchies

Drill down adds a finer level of detail. Drill up regroups it at a higher level.

Year → Quarter → Month → Day

Use + and − to move between the available levels.

In this example, all 24 monthly rows stay included. A year total splits into quarters, then months; the total stays unchanged.

For discrete dates, + adds the next level while keeping its parent.

Drilling down is different from filtering to one year.

Tableau Help9 / 33
Visual Analytics in TableauIA342 · Week 9

Date Grouping — MONTH vs YEAR + MONTH

MONTH(Order Date) alone groups all January records together, irrespective of year.

YEAR(Order Date) + MONTH(Order Date) creates two levels of discrete headers: Year, then Month.

Read the Columns shelf and the header structure together. January under 2024 is a different group from January under 2025.

Both examples are discrete. The added Year grouping—not a color change—separates the years.

A month-level date value can also retain the year in one field. Blue/green alone does not determine which date components are retained.

Drill Down — A Custom Hierarchy

A hierarchy organizes dimensions into an ordered path from summary to detail.

CLARITY → IDNO

At CLARITY level, one bar summarizes a category. Expanding adds a bar for each ID within that category.

Collapsing recomputes the average from those records. It does not sum the child prices or remove them.

Drill down changes the grouping level.
A filter changes the included subset.

Diamonds has no date field. The same hierarchical idea applies to categorical dimensions.

Sort — Field and Nested Sorts

Sort changes member order while leaving their aggregate values unchanged.

Here the outer dimension is COLOR; the inner dimension is CLARITY. The measure is AVG(PRICE).

Field sort: one CLARITY ordering computed over the retained records, repeated in each COLOR pane.

Nested sort: a separate ranking of CLARITY inside each COLOR pane.

The same label can have a different position in each pane under a nested sort.

Group — Combine Category Members

A Group creates a new categorical dimension by assigning several existing members to one label.

VS1 + VS2 → VS

The grouped chart combines the underlying records and recomputes the measure.

It does not delete rows or turn distinct diamonds into duplicate records.

Group result: a category label.
Set result: IN / OUT membership.

The merged average weights every source row equally. Bins and rule-based calculated categories are other grouping techniques—not the Group command itself.

Set — Top 5 by Price

A Set identifies a subset of dimension members. Each ID is IN or OUT.

One example: Top 5 by Price

Rank IDNO members by AVG(PRICE). The five highest belong to the set.

Use that membership on Color: the five members stand out; the others remain visible.

The set contains IDs, not five new price categories. It does not merge those five marks.

In Tableau Online, use the available Create Set workflow to select members. The Tableau screenshot uses a fixed set named big; the HTML example demonstrates a separate Top 5 membership rule. Put a set on Color to see IN/OUT.

Filters — Levels and Execution Order

A filter limits the data or results used in an analysis. Its level determines when the restriction is applied.

Execution order ↓What this level doesExample
1Extract filterLimits the rows copied into an extract when it is built.Keep only a selected date range in the extract.
2Data source filterRestricts rows available to worksheets using that source.COVID source: counts ≥ 0.
3Context filterDefines a worksheet subset before dependent filters.GIA first, then Top 5 within GIA.
4Dimension filterSelects dimension members before the view's aggregation.Keep CLARITY = VS1.
5Measure filterTests aggregated measures at the view's level of detail.Keep AVG(PRICE) > 2,500.
6Table calculation filterHides marks after table calculations; their input data stay included.Hide a calculated result without recomputing the others.

The level—not the order in which you add filters—determines execution.

Tableau Help: Order of operations · Context filters20 / 33
Visual Analytics in TableauIA342 · Week 9

Filters — Aggregation and Comparison

When a continuous measure such as PRICE is dragged to Filters, Tableau asks two questions: what values are tested? and which results pass?

1. Aggregation — what is tested?

  • All Values: individual diamond PRICE values (row-level).
  • Average: AVG(PRICE) for each group in the view.
  • Sum: SUM(PRICE) for each group; group size matters.

2. Comparison — which values pass?

  • Range of Values: between 2,000 and 4,000 (inclusive).
  • At Least: 2,500 or higher.
  • At Most: 2,500 or lower.
  • Special: null / non-null values.
PRICE filter: At Least 2,500What remains if the view groups by CLARITY?Effect
All ValuesOnly diamonds with PRICE ≥ 2,500 contribute to each CLARITY group.Row-level filtering
AverageOnly CLARITY groups with AVG(PRICE) ≥ 2,500 remain; their contributing records are still used in the average.Aggregate measure filtering

Contrast: a dimension filter such as CLARITY = VS1 selects category members before the view is aggregated. Aggregation and comparison are settings for a quantitative filter, not new stages in Slide 20.

Tableau Help: Filtering measures · Order of operations

Trend Lines — Fit the Displayed Data

A linear trend line fits:

fitted PRICE = intercept + slope × WEIGHT

Slope summarizes the direction and rate of change. R² summarizes fit to these plotted values; it is not proof of causation.

In Tableau

Keep IDNO on Detail. Remove categorical Color for one overall fit, then use Analytics → Trend Line → Linear.

Filter by RATER to recompute the fit. In Tableau, use one fit without color factors, allow a free intercept, and turn off confidence bands to match this example.

Reference Lines — Value and Scope

A reference line locates a benchmark on a continuous axis. Unlike a trend line, it does not fit the relationship between two measures.

Choose the reference value

  • Constant: a specified value, such as WEIGHT = 1.0.
  • Statistic: a mean or median of the relevant plotted values.
  • Parameter: a value the viewer controls.

A reference band covers an interval; a distribution band uses statistical ranges.

Choose its scope

Scope How many references?
Entire Table One for the view
Per Pane One for each pane
Per Cell One for each cell

In Price vs Weight, add a horizontal mean-PRICE line. Then add RATER to Columns and compare Entire Table with Per Pane.

An average of displayed group marks may differ from the overall row-level mean when group sizes differ. At the IDNO level here, each mark corresponds to one record.

Parameters — One Adjustable Value

A parameter stores one current number, text value, or date.

It affects a view only through an object that uses it.

Here price level controls a reference line and this category:

IF [PRICE] > [price level] THEN
  'Above threshold'
ELSE
  'At or below threshold'
END

One number → two effects.
The record values stay unchanged.

Actions — Connect Interaction to Results

An action connects a user's interaction in a source view to a defined response in a target.

USER INTERACTIONSelect · Hover · Menu
→
ACTION RULEWhat should change?
→
TARGETA view, a set, or a parameter
Action typeTargetExample result
FilterAnother worksheetSelect a state → show only that state's counties.
Change Set ValuesAn existing setSelect counties → update membership; a calculation or Color uses the set.
Change ParameterAn existing parameterSelect a price → update price level → move its reference line.

Other actions highlight related marks or navigate to a sheet or URL.

Action = trigger + target + response. Groups supply category values; they are not a separate action type.

Tooltips — Detail and a Filtered View

For an ordinary tooltip, use Marks → Tooltip → Insert to include IDNO, PRICE, WEIGHT, CLARITY, and RATER.

Viz in Tooltip displays a filtered image of another worksheet—not a second interactive worksheet:

source mark → filter fields → target view

The county bar supplies its geographic identity. The target line chart recomputes that county's weekly values.

Turn off the filter in this example: every source bar then shows the same combined series.

Data Guide and Explain Data

Data Guide provides view context: filters, fields, summaries, and detected outliers.

Explain Data evaluates statistical explanations for a selected mark. It does not establish the cause of the observed result.

Use Data Guide where enabled; explanations vary with the view and selection.

In Tableau

  1. Restore CLARITY on Rows and AVG(PRICE) on Columns.
  2. Select IF and open Data Guide.
  3. Inspect the proposed contributing measures.
  4. Compare the underlying WEIGHT and PRICE values and active filters.
